title: I Tested 5 Claude AI Side Hustles — Only These Actually Made Money
summary: A YouTube coach recounts failed FBA, dropshipping, agency and flipping attempts, and argues an owned audience built with AI-scripted videos is the foundation that makes any side hustle pay.

assertions.quote: Amazon FBA, drop shipping, SMMA, flipping, these are not bad business models.
Without it, every business is a great store in the middle of the desert. Nobody walks by and nobody buys

verdicts.note: Customer acquisition is the dominant cost in online business, but many profitable stores run on paid traffic without an audience; the audience framing suits a YouTube coach.

assertions.quote: Then Meta jacked up the CPMs. Other people started copying me, selling the exact same products, and it became a race to the bottom.

verdicts.note: Low barriers to entry mean any winning product is cloned within weeks, and ad auctions price the margin away; this is the standard dropshipping failure mode.

assertions.quote: Even when SMMA works, it is a job. This is not a side hustle.

verdicts.note: Agency work is client services with ongoing delivery and churn; it is a legitimate business but has none of the passive-income properties pitched.

assertions.quote: Flipping only works if somebody else already wants what you're selling.

verdicts.note: Resale depends on existing demand and skilled flippers do develop an edge, but for beginners outcomes are dominated by timing.

assertions.quote: someone with 60,000 subscribers in the right niche is pulling 80 grand a month.

verdicts.note: Niche B2B and career channels do monetise far better per view, but the cited figures are selected client anecdotes, not typical outcomes.
Revenue per view varies many-fold by niche, so this can happen, but the cited figures are selected anecdotes.

assertions.quote: the biggest beginner barrier, writing the scripts, is gone.

verdicts.note: AI does cut scripting time, but discoverability, retention and on-camera skill remain the binding constraints and AI lowers the barrier for competitors equally.
Discoverability and retention, not scripts, are the binding constraints, and AI lowers the scripting barrier for every competitor equally.

assertions.quote: You build the thing once and it sells while you sleep for years.

verdicts.note: Some evergreen products do earn for years, but most digital products sell almost nothing without continual promotion; the median outcome is near zero.
Most digital products sell almost nothing without continual promotion, so passive income for years is the rare case.

assertions.quote: We have gotten six figure sales from videos that we posted over 5 years ago.

verdicts.note: Evergreen search-driven videos do keep earning, but most videos decay to near-zero views within weeks; compounding applies to a minority of channels.
Evergreen search-driven videos do keep earning, but most videos decay quickly, so compounding holds only for a minority of channels.

assertions.quote: by day 29, he had his first $214 in a single day from AdSense. So, so he went from zero to a full-time income.
I'd met influencers and YouTubers that had millions of subscribers and millions of followers and were completely broke.
